definitions.explanation: A medical professional who diagnoses and treats patients.

examples.english: I want to become a doctor.

examples.japanese: {熱|ねつ}があるので、{医者|いしゃ}に{診|み}てもらった。
examples.english: I had a fever, so I had a doctor examine me.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}は「もっと{休|やす}んでください」と{言|い}った。
お{腹|なか}が{痛|いた}くて{医者|いしゃ}に{行|い}ったら、{薬|くすり}をもらった。
examples.english: I went to the doctor because my stomach hurt, and I received medicine.

notes:
{医者|いしゃ} is the everyday word for 'doctor' in Japanese.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {医者|いしゃ}に{行|い}く: to go to the doctor
- {医者|いしゃ}に{診|み}てもらう: to be examined by a doctor
- {医者|いしゃ}に{掛|か}かる: to see a doctor (for treatment)
- {医者|いしゃ}になる: to become a doctor

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- お{医者|いしゃ}さん: doctor (polite, child-friendly — the most common spoken form)
- {医者|いしゃ}: doctor (neutral)
- {医師|いし}: physician (formal/official — used in documents, news, and legal contexts)

SPECIALISTS:
- {歯医者|はいしゃ}: dentist
- {獣医|じゅうい}: veterinarian
- {名医|めいい}: renowned doctor

PROVERB:
{医者|いしゃ}の{不養生|ふようじょう}: the doctor neglects their own health (equivalent to 'the cobbler's children have no shoes')
